origin.claim: Binary markets historically overprice very unlikely outcomes (the longshot bias) and underprice near-certain ones, so buying the NO side of an extreme YES price has a positive expected value if the bias is present.
origin.status: hypothesis under test - the competition is the test

rules.entry: YES mid <= 0.10, spread <= 3 cents, at least 2 hours to close, top-3 liquidity strikes only.
rules.exit: No exit: positions are held to settlement, because the thesis is about the settlement distribution.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped at 25% of the resting depth within 2 cents of the offer.

strategies.thesis: Buy NO on commodity event contracts whose YES price is at or below 10 cents. If the longshot bias exists in Kalshi commodity ladders, the average NO leg should be profitable on a large number of observations; if the bias does not exist, this strategy loses and the leaderboard will show it.

origin.claim: The same bias that overprices longshots underprices near-certain outcomes; buying NO at 90c+ YES prices collects a small premium with a large loss tail.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: YES mid >= 0.90, spread <= 3 cents, closes within 48 hours.
rules.exit: No exit: held to settlement.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by verified resting depth.

strategies.thesis: Buy NO where YES is already at or above 90 cents and the contract closes within two days. This is the mirror image of the longshot fade: it wins often and loses big occasionally, which is exactly the return profile a highest-return-only competition is allowed to take.

origin.claim: Kalshi charges no maker fee on standard series, so resting inside a wide commodity spread captures the bid-ask spread at zero commission if it gets filled.
origin.status: structural - no forecast required

rules.entry: Spread >= 3 cents, resting bid at best bid + 1 cent, never crossing the offer.
rules.exit: Working orders expire after the configured TTL; positions are marked to the opposite side of the book.
rules.sizing: One resting order per market, size from verified depth at the resting price.

strategies.thesis: Rest passive bids one cent inside the spread on the most liquid commodity contracts and rely on the exchange order flow to cross them. The maker fee multiplier is zero for standard series per the official fee schedule, so a fill at the resting price is pure spread capture.

origin.claim: Single-day price gaps in thin commodity ladders often overshoot and partially retrace, because the gap is driven by order-flow rather than information.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: Last completed daily candle change >= 4 standard deviations of the series history, trade the opposite direction.
rules.exit: Exit when the mid returns to within half the gap, or when the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by verified depth.

strategies.thesis: When a series candle history shows a move of more than four standard deviations of its own daily changes, take the opposite side of that move in the front ladder. Measured entirely from Kalshi's own official candle payload.

origin.claim: Cheap YES contracts that are already trending up can keep trending when the underlying commodity is moving, giving convex payoffs; this is the explicit counter-hypothesis to the longshot fade.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: YES mid <= 0.10, 5-day candle momentum > 0, spread <= 3 cents.
rules.exit: Exit when 5-day momentum turns negative or the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by depth.

strategies.thesis: Buy YES at 10 cents or less only when the series own official candle history is trending up. This strategy is deliberately the opposite bet to @fade-the-crowd, so the leaderboard measures which view of cheap contracts is right.

origin.claim: If two strikes of the same series imply a probability ordering that contradicts the strike ordering, buying the cheap leg and the NO of the rich leg is a structural arbitrage.
origin.status: structural - no forecast required

rules.entry: Monotonicity violation of at least 2 cents between two strikes of the same series and expiry.
rules.exit: Held to settlement (the two legs converge by construction).
rules.sizing: Target notional per leg, capped by depth.

strategies.thesis: Within one series and one expiry, the YES price must fall as the strike rises (for greater-than markets). When the published book violates that ordering by more than the configured tolerance, buy the underpriced YES leg and the NO of the overpriced leg.

origin.claim: Energy event contracts follow the underlying crude complex with a lag; the exchange own candle history is a verified, free proxy for that trend.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: |5-day candle momentum| >= 2%, enter in the direction of the trend, YES mid between 0.2 and 0.6.
rules.exit: Exit when momentum flips sign or the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by depth.

strategies.thesis: Trade the Kalshi WTI/Brent ladders in the direction of the verified trend in the same series own official candle history, taking the side whose price is closest to a coin flip so that a correct directional call pays multiples.

origin.claim: Listed metal perpetuals trend after their own mark price moves when the underlying spot market is closed, because the perpetual must carry the overnight move.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: Price changed since the previous committed snapshot, with a live two-sided quote.
rules.exit: Exit when the direction of the last change flips.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by a share of published 24h notional volume.

strategies.thesis: Take the direction of the last verified move in each Kalshi metal perpetual and hold it, re-evaluating on every snapshot. The perpetual is the only instrument in this project that trades continuously, so it is where an overnight trend can actually be captured.

origin.claim: Cross-sectional momentum in metals futures is a long-documented effect; this strategy simply buys the strongest and shorts the weakest contract it can actually price.
origin.status: hypothesis under test with a verified, free official data feed

rules.entry: 20-observation settlement momentum, long the top mover and short the bottom mover on each side when |momentum| >= 1%.
rules.exit: Exit when the momentum flips sign.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Rank the MOEX metal futures by their official settlement momentum over the cached history window and take the extremes, long the strongest and short the weakest. Trades only when the exchange publishes both a live quote and USD valuation inputs.

origin.claim: The spread between two expiries of the same commodity is a financing/storage carry; when its annualised value exceeds the exchange-published round-trip cost, the carry is capturable.
origin.status: structural - measured, not forecast

rules.entry: Annualised calendar spread >= 12% after measured round-trip fees.
rules.exit: Exit when the annualised spread compresses below 4%, or when either contract is within 5 days of expiry.
rules.sizing: Target notional per leg, capped by both contracts published liquidity.

strategies.thesis: Buy the near expiry and sell the far expiry (or the reverse) whenever the annualised spread between the official mid prices exceeds the exchange published round-trip fee converted at the official USD/RUB rate. Both legs are real orders with real fees.

origin.claim: Soft-commodity futures on MOEX trade in long supply-driven trends that are visible in their own official settlement history.
origin.status: hypothesis under test

rules.entry: 15-observation settlement momentum, |momentum| >= 1.5%.
rules.exit: Exit when the momentum flips sign.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Follow the official settlement trend in MOEX soft commodities and grains, taking the strongest movers on each side and holding while the trend persists.

strategies.market_type: Cross-venue: Kalshi perpetual future vs exchange-listed future

origin.claim: A 24/7 listed perpetual and a session-based futures contract on the same metal cannot diverge indefinitely; when the basis exceeds its own cost of carry, the two must converge. The MOEX premium/discount to the world metal price since 2022 is a documented, persistent phenomenon.

sources.label: Kalshi perp contract specification (official help centre: contract size in underlying units)
MOEX ISS security description endpoint (LOTSIZE / quotation UNIT / FACEUNIT)

origin.status: structural - two real legs on two real venues, unit-normalised from official fields

rules.entry: Normalised basis >= 0.5% between the perpetual (USD/oz via contract_size) and the MOEX front future (USD/oz via official UNIT/LOT SIZE).
rules.exit: Exit when the basis compresses below 0.1%, or when either leg loses its verified quote or normalisation inputs.
rules.sizing: Target notional per leg, capped by each venue published liquidity.

sizing.sizing_note: Per-leg target notional. It must exceed the value of one MOEX metal contract (GOLD-12.26 lot = 1 troy ounce, quoted USD/oz, ~$4,400 per contract on 2026-09-22) or the minimum size is zero contracts and no trade can be placed.

strategies.thesis: Compare the Kalshi metal perpetual (price / contract_size = USD per ounce) with the front MOEX future on the same metal (mid = USD per ounce when UNIT=USD). When the normalised basis is large enough to cover both venues fees, buy the cheaper venue and sell the more expensive one. Both legs are simulated with their own venue fill model.

origin.claim: Standing-book imbalance is a classic order-flow signal: when resting depth is heavily concentrated on one side, the next short-horizon move is disproportionately in that side's direction. Prediction-market strategy write-ups list flow/liquidity signals among the recurring edges.

sources.label: Prediction-market strategy synthesis (flow and liquidity signals)

origin.status: hypothesis under test - the competition is the test

rules.entry: Depth ratio >= 70% or <= 30% on visible book depth, spread <= 3 cents, YES mid between 0.15 and 0.85, at least 2 hours to close.
rules.exit: Exit when the depth ratio crosses back through 50% or the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped at 25% of the resting depth within 2 cents of the offer.

strategies.thesis: Trade in the direction of the heavily unbalanced resting book: when the official order book shows at least 70% of visible depth on one side and the spread is tight, buy that side, betting that the resting liquidity reflects informed order flow.

origin.claim: A perpetual's book is anchored to the exchange-published mark/index price: deviations are driven by transient order flow and tend to decay back toward the mark. Kalshi publishes the mark (settlement mark price) for every perpetual in the same payload as the book.
origin.status: structural - the anchor is published by the exchange itself

rules.entry: |perp mid / exchange mark - 1| >= 0.30%, with a live two-sided book; trade toward the mark.
rules.exit: Exit when the deviation decays below 0.08% or the two-sided quote disappears.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by a share of published 24h notional volume.

strategies.thesis: When the Kalshi perpetual mid deviates from the exchange-published mark price by 0.3% or more, trade back toward the mark; exit when the deviation decays below 0.08%. Both the deviation and its anchor come from the exchange payload in the same snapshot.

origin.claim: Energy futures trend on supply shocks: crude, products and gas move in multi-week runs that their own settlement history makes measurable. MOEX lists WTI, Brent, natural gas (NG/NGM/TTF), diesel and AI-92/95 gasoline contracts, all readable from the official ISS API.
origin.status: hypothesis under test on contracts verified in the exchange listing on 2026-09-22

rules.entry: 15-observation settlement momentum, |momentum| >= 1.5%.
rules.exit: Exit when the momentum flips sign.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Follow the official settlement trend in MOEX energy futures - crude (WTI, Brent), products (diesel, AI-92/95 gasoline) and gas (NG, NGM, TTF) - taking the strongest movers on each side and holding while the trend persists.

origin.claim: Channel (Donchian) breakout rules - buy a 20-period high, sell a 20-period low, exit on the opposite 10-period extreme - are the public-domain Turtle trading rules, among the most documented systematic futures strategies.

sources.label: Original Turtle Trading rules (public domain, official release by the authors)

origin.status: documented rule, forward-tested here on official MOEX settlements

rules.entry: Daily settlement CLOSE crosses above the prior 20-observation high (long) or below the prior 20-observation low (short).
rules.exit: Close crosses the opposite 10-observation extreme.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Run the classic 20/10 channel breakout on MOEX metals futures using only the exchange's official daily settlement history: buy the 20-day high breakout, short the 20-day low breakout, exit on the opposite 10-day extreme.

origin.claim: Short-horizon reversal: abrupt one-interval price jumps in thin binary books routinely overshoot because the first wave of flow consumes several levels; prediction-market write-ups treat post-jump entries as a recurring, testable pattern.
origin.status: hypothesis under test - tick-to-tick, on official snapshot mids only

rules.entry: |mid change between the previous committed snapshot and this one| >= 6 cents, spread <= 4 cents, at least 2 hours to close, mid between 0.08 and 0.92.
rules.exit: Exit when the mid retraces half of the measured jump, or the market closes.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by verified depth.

strategies.thesis: When a contract's official mid moves by 6 cents or more between two consecutive verified snapshots, take the opposite side: fade the jump. Deliberately distinct from @vol-crusher (which fades daily-candle extremes from the exchange candle history), this acts on tick-to-tick snapshot moves.

origin.claim: FX futures on MOEX FORTS (USD/RUB "Si", CNY/RUB) trend over multi-week stretches of central-bank policy and flows; the official settlement history makes the trend measurable without any forecast.
origin.status: hypothesis under test on contracts verified in the exchange listing on 2026-09-22

rules.entry: 15-observation settlement momentum, |momentum| >= 1.5%.
rules.exit: Exit when the momentum flips sign.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Follow the official settlement trend in MOEX FX futures - the USD/RUB and CNY/RUB contracts - taking the strongest movers and holding while the trend persists. Same measured-momentum rule as the energy desk, applied to the FX sector the brief requires the universe to cover.

origin.claim: Equity-index futures are the canonical momentum market: index-level trends persist over weeks, and momentum rules on index futures are among the most replicated results in the literature. MOEX FORTS lists IMOEX, RTS, Nasdaq-100 and S&P 500 index futures through the same keyless ISS API.
origin.status: hypothesis under test on contracts verified in the exchange listing on 2026-09-22

rules.entry: 15-observation settlement momentum, |momentum| >= 2.0%.
rules.exit: Exit when the momentum flips sign.
rules.sizing: Target notional, capped by published volume and open interest.

strategies.thesis: Trade the official settlement momentum in MOEX equity-index futures - IMOEX (MIX), RTS, Nasdaq-100 (NASD) and S&P 500 (SPYF) - long the 15-observation winners, short the losers, and exit when the momentum flips. The index sector is one of the market types the brief requires the universe to cover.

origin.claim: The spread between near and far rate futures is the market's own estimate of the future short rate; when its annualised value exceeds the round-trip cost, the carry is capturable. MOEX FORTS lists RUONIA and 1MFR rate futures through the same keyless ISS API.
origin.status: structural - measured, not forecast

rules.entry: Annualised calendar spread >= 8% after measured round-trip fees.
rules.exit: Exit when the annualised spread compresses below 3%, or when either contract is within 5 days of expiry.
rules.sizing: Target notional per leg, sized against the exchange-published lot notional (1,000,000 RUB per RUONIA/1MFR contract per the official specification) and capped by both contracts published liquidity.

strategies.thesis: Buy the near expiry and sell the far expiry (or the reverse) of the same MOEX rate future whenever the annualised spread between the official mid prices exceeds the exchange-published round-trip fee. The interest-rate sector is one of the market types the brief requires the universe to cover; the rule is the calendar-carry rule applied to the rate curve.
